findings.status: open — structural, owned by TASK-388's naming convention, not by this card
findings.severity: medium (design), zero impact on this card's correctness
findings.finding: the receipt naming convention is unsatisfiable by construction whenever the card points at its own receipt by filename.
findings.why: the filename embeds sha256(card), and the card's bytes embed the filename. Naming the receipt after the final card's digest therefore changes the final card's digest.
findings.demonstration: the card at 19860c2 digests to 66e0c237... while its quality-review-receipt: line still names done-review-03475cc9....json. Rewriting only that line to name done-review-66e0c237....json makes the card digest to 8343f407e58d8380fb3ca2eb996f992ea82e3f8c42e8083b506aea74a94d70f5 — a third value. Each re-pin invalidates itself. This is a fixed-point requirement, not a workflow awkwardness, and no amount of re-issuing converges.
findings.resolution: pick one of two coherent readings. (a) The digest names the REVISION THAT WAS REVIEWED, and is not expected to equal the current card — this receipt adopts (a). (b) Drop the digest from the filename and carry it as a field inside the receipt, leaving the pointer stable. (a) costs one sentence in TASK-388; (b) costs a rename convention.
findings.consequence-for-this-close: if the lead updates the card's pointer to this receipt's new filename, the card's final digest becomes 8343f407..., stated here in advance so the drift is recorded rather than discovered later. That prediction is the receipt-level version of F5's remedy: name the basis, do not let the number rot silently.

canonical-digest-probe.conclusion: the CE canonical review digest is NOT sha256 over the file bytes. Two further probes — one changing only a frontmatter value, one changing only a body line — each moved the canonical digest, so it covers card content including frontmatter. A canonical digest read out of a mutated copy therefore pins the mutated copy, not this card.
canonical-digest-probe.correction-to-prior-record: this supersedes the blanket claim that a canonical digest cannot be produced here. It can be produced for any card the validator actually checks — a done card declaring blocks:. What cannot be produced is a canonical digest for a card the validator skips, which is this card's situation at b4b1f20.
